name: EXP
description: EXP returns e raised to the power of a given number, where e is the base of the natural logarithm (approximately 2.71828182845904).
tldr: Returns e raised to a power.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The exponent to which e is raised.

basicExample.description: e raised to the power of 1
basicExample.explanation: e¹ equals the constant e, about 2.71828.

advancedExamples.title: Inverse relationship with LN
advancedExamples.description: LN and EXP cancel each other.
advancedExamples.explanation: Taking the natural log of e³ returns 3.

howItWorks: EXP computes e^number, where e ≈ 2.71828182845904. It is the inverse of LN: LN(EXP(x)) = x and EXP(LN(x)) = x (for x > 0).

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the result.

limitations: Very large exponents overflow to #NUM! (e.g. EXP(710) and above).
Results are floating-point approximations of e.
EXP only computes powers of e; use POWER for other bases.

commonErrors.cause: The exponent is too large, causing overflow.
commonErrors.fix: Use a smaller exponent or scale the calculation.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: EXP works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: What is e?
faq.answer: e is Euler's number, approximately 2.71828182845904, the base of natural logarithms.

faq.question: How do I raise other numbers to a power?
faq.answer: Use POWER(base, exponent) or the ^ operator; EXP only raises e.

faq.question: Why does EXP(LN(x)) equal x?
faq.answer: EXP and LN are inverse functions, so they cancel each other for positive x.
